solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keeps it in the family

parts.note: read literally, keeping something in the family sounds like discretion, but here it means breeding only with close relatives

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly keeps a matter private among relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests keeping a secret or business among kin; the cryptic reading is literal mating within the family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that mate with close relatives, keeping the bloodline within one family, are said to do this.

clue.text: Bug fashionable clique

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
a sect is a small exclusive group, a clique

explanation.surface: A bug spreads through a trendy social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an everyday synonym for a creepy-crawly with six legs.

clue.text: Pointed comments about reconstruction of Inca towers

indicators.note: the barbed remarks go about, that is surround, the reworked letters

parts.note: barbs are pointed, wounding remarks

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds the word Inca in a new order

explanation.surface: Sharp remarks are made about rebuilding some Inca towers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed comments' tempts as the definition, but towers is it; 'reconstruction of' signals the anagram and 'about' the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbicans are fortified outer towers guarding a gate or bridge of a castle.

clue.text: Fighting calls for signs of commitment

parts.note: an engagement is a battle, a spell of fighting
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Battle cries are taken as tokens of loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: These pieces of jewellery are given as tokens that a couple has promised to marry.

clue.text: Arriving in port — important man on board under doctor

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: the king is the most important piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A ship comes in with a VIP on deck below the ship's doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but the board is a chessboard and the important man is its king.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is docking is coming in to berth at a quay in harbour.

clue.text: High finish hurt feelings

parts.note: meat that is high has gone off
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A lofty ending upsets someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To give offence is to hurt someone's feelings, so the verb phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Forms of society?

parts.note: forms are school classes, and society here is high society, so these are classes in an establishment teaching social graces

explanation.surface: A question about the various structures a society can take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' reads as types or structures; in British schools a form is a class year.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a private school polishes young women in etiquette for entry into high society.

clue.text: Communication trouble following contents of memo

indicators.note: the trouble comes after the inner letters of memo
the contents of a word are its letters without the outer ones

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A message causes problems after someone reads what the memo says.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a common form of written communication.

clue.text: Humiliated theologian outside — agreed to differ

indicators.note: the theologian's letters sit outside, around the reworked word

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: the letters of agreed are made to differ from their order

explanation.surface: A humbled churchman agrees to disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'agreed to differ' is a stock phrase; here 'to differ' signals an anagram and 'outside' places the theologian around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be degraded is to be brought low in dignity, humiliated.

clue.text: Officers' material protecting setter

indicators.note: the material wraps round and so protects the setter

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton fabric
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Officers' cloth shields the compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers and sheriffs are men of the law; the possessive mark is ignored.

clue.text: Show indifference to quiet carpeting

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rug is a piece of carpeting

explanation.surface: Someone is unbothered by being told off for noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' suggests a telling-off but here it is a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is the gesture that signals not caring.

clue.text: Joined Labour Party

parts.note: not a political membership but a party of prisoners joined by fetters and doing forced labour

explanation.surface: Someone became a member of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest British politics; read as joined (linked) labour party (work group).
explanation.definitionFit: A group of convicts fettered together to do outdoor work is described here.

clue.text: Hang on — the movie's a wrap!

parts.note: to cling is to hang on
a film is a movie

explanation.surface: A director calls an end to the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a wrap' is film talk for finishing filming; here a wrap is food packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin plastic sheeting is used to wrap food.

clue.text: Regrettably comes back carrying a bit of salad dressing

indicators.note: the reversed word carries, that is holds, the letter inside it
coming back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: alas expresses regret

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone returns with a scrap of salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns ALAS into SALA, and 'carrying' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy tomato sauce is used as a dressing or dip.

clue.text: Playboy, for example, is hopping mad to be hugged by prisoner

indicators.note: the prisoner surrounds, hugs, the reworked letters

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

indicators.note: hopping jumbles the letters of mad

explanation.surface: A womaniser, furious, gets an embrace from a convict.
explanation.walkthrough: Playboy here is the magazine title, not a rake; 'hopping' signals the anagram the convict hugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is a men's magazine, an example of the genre aimed at young men.

clue.text: Offensive racket surrounding return of doctor

indicators.note: the racket goes round the reversed doctor

parts.note: a racket is a din, noise

indicators.note: return means the doctor's letters come backwards

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer

explanation.surface: An obnoxious din envelops a doctor's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor; 'return of' turns it to OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisome is foul or disgusting, so offensive.

clue.text: Exercises incorporated into speech surgery

indicators.note: the exercises are put inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Physical drills are worked into a lecture on surgical practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical procedure on a patient is called an operation.

clue.text: A bit of water for Spooner's sewage work?

indicators.note: Spooner's swaps the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a drain carries sewage
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A question about a single drop of water from a sewage plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of rain is a small bit of water.

clue.text: Agrees to speak of climbs

indicators.note: to speak of means the word for climbs is said out loud

parts.note: ascents are climbs

explanation.surface: Someone consents to talk about mountain climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To give assent is to consent, so the verb is a synonym of agrees.

clue.text: Replaced warship on bottom of sea

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel of war
the seabed is the bottom of the sea

explanation.surface: A submarine settled on the ocean floor is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' places the first piece over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a player who is subbed is replaced by a substitute.

clue.text: Report of hardship experienced by scaffolder

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: rigour is hardship or severity

explanation.surface: A building worker gives an account of tough times.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger erects scaffolding or rigging, so a scaffolder.

clue.text: Set aside such modesty

explanation.surface: Someone puts aside such shyness.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means keep back; as a noun it means restrained, modest behaviour.

clue.text: Reacts in shock and begins

definitions.meaning: to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: Someone jumps in surprise and gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to jump with fright and to commence.

clue.text: The lowest point revealed in a directive?

indicators.note: the answer is shown within the run of letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A question whether rock bottom is disclosed in an official order.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom-most point, opposite the zenith.

clue.text: Design nothing right after Christmas?

indicators.note: the nothing and right come after the Christmas month

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A design with nothing right once the festive season is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas stands for its month, December, shortened to DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decorative design and furnishing of a room.

clue.text: Skill required for a presidential yacht?

definitions.meaning: outdoor survival skill in the wild
a boat belonging to one of the Presidents Bush

explanation.surface: Expertise is needed to handle the President's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the craft of surviving in the bush, a skill; read differently, a boat of Bush.

clue.text: One tells of cut on rear going bad

indicators.note: the words go bad, spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A storyteller talks of a cut on the rear turning septic.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells stories skilfully.

clue.text: Willow is pinker when pollarded

indicators.note: pollarding cuts off a tree's top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rosier means pinker

explanation.surface: A willow tree looks pinker after its crown is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollarding fits the willow surface: willows are commonly pollarded.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow used for basketry.

clue.text: Copper hears about partial sentence

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, P

indicators.note: about means the letters of hears are moved around

explanation.surface: A policeman hears about a reduced jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'sentence' suggest police and prison; copper is the coin, penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words forming part of a sentence.

clue.text: Pins and needles may raise them

definitions.text: Pins and needles may raise them

parts.words: Pins and needles may raise them
parts.note: not a tingling sensation but a dressmaker's pins and sewing needles taking up the bottom of a skirt

explanation.surface: Tingling in the limbs may cause something to go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins and needles' suggests numbness; here they are sewing tools shortening a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressmakers raise the bottom edges of skirts by pinning and sewing them up.
